sections.content:
My relationship with aesthetics changed in the master. Since my bachelor, making [a 3D game](/interactive-media-project), 270 hours between two people, every model and shader our own, far beyond the assignment, focussed mainly on the visual end result (\ref{interactive-media}).

The [AIBPO](/aesthetics-of-ai-data) project is where my shift in perspective became most visible. The main aesthetic goal wasn't to make something look good, it was to make an audience feel the discomfort of a system we were critiquing. Ambiguity and staged authority became intentional design materials. The real limitation is that a live performance leaves almost nothing behind, the intent is inaccessible to anyone who wasn't in the room.

The shift is less about skill and more about what I was asking aesthetics to do: execution in one case, framing in the other.

Level: intermediate. I can use aesthetics as framing rather than only execution, while still building the critical perspective to question my own instincts.
